newsitem.title: UK: UK could regain control over farms, fish - Howard.
newsitem.headline: UK could regain control over farms, fish - Howard.

text.p: Michael Howard, the candidate for the leadership of Britain's Conservatives savaged by a colleague in parliament on Monday, has begun his fightback by calling for a far more flexible European Union.

Howard, whose bid to replace John Major was dealt a blow by Ann Widdecombe's claims that he misled parliament, said in a pamphlet that such an arrangement could mean Britain regaining control over both fisheries and farming policy.

The pamphlet, published by the Centre for Policy Studies think-tank, said the so-called variable geometry approach "will prevent the political earthquake which would undoubtedly result from trying to follow the federal route".
"Variable geometry could allow for the repatriation of a number of areas of policy where there is no practical need for pan-European action," Howard wrote.
One example he cited was controls over drinking water standards, which are currently set in Brussels.
"Another example...is the reassertion of national jurisdiction over fishing grounds -- out to a 200 mile limit," he said.
In the longer term, he added, European Union member states could resume control over farm policy, becoming free to provide direct support to farmers' incomes.
"The repatriation of agriculture may appear to be an ambitious aim," Howard wrote.

"But the twin pressures of eastward enlargement (of the EU) and world trade liberalisation will force the EU to restructure the existing system. These pressures could give Britain the opportunity to retrieve control of its own farming policy." -- London Newsroom +44 171 54277767
